docs.title: Welcome to ASRC Photonics Shared Facility
docs.text:
The Photonics Shared Facility at the CUNY Advanced Science Research Center provides researchers with access to state-of-the-art optical instrumentation, expert training, and collaborative opportunities.

Here you’ll find:

🔬 Equipment – access to advanced optical tools 📘 How-to guides – becoming a user & lab policies 🎓 Internships – opportunities for students to learn and grow 📅 Events – workshops, talks, and community activities 📬 Contact – connect with us anytime

🚀 Start by exploring our Howto section or checking out the Equipment.

docs.title: Become a user
docs.text:
Steps to become the photonics facility user:

  1. Fill out and submit the ASRC Facility New User Application.
  2. Complete the EHOS Lab Safety Training.
  3. Complete the Photonics Facility Orientation.
  4. Get an ASRC ID.
  5. Schedule tool training.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The ASRC Photonics Shared Facility hosts students at various levels — from high-school to undergraduate — to provide hands-on research experience in optics and photonics.

Through summer programs, internships, and mentorship opportunities, students gain exposure to advanced equipment, collaborative projects, and the excitement of scientific discovery.

• Melanie Choca (LaGuardia Internship, continues in the Fall 2025 through ASRC CAT stipend) Working on PECVD SiO2 spacer deposition and optical characterization of stacked metalenses.

  • Adi Mazumdar (LaGuardia Internship) Worked on SiC reactive ion etching recipe for nanostructures.

  • Anna Luo (NYU GSTEM Internship) Worked on Automated 2D mapping in transmission measurements using python.

  • Lilah Anders (NYU GSTEM Internship) Worked on COMSOL modeling of whispering gallery mode resonators.

  • Ariana Ahmad (CUNY VSURF Internship) Worked on Reflection measurements of metasurfaces for biosensing applications.

  • Ayisha Yankey (Nordtech/Griffis Institute Internship) Worked on Python automation scripts for controlling optical stages and cameras.

  • Tomas Gonsalez (Nordtech/Griffis Institute Internship) Worked on Microtransmission measurements of metasurfaces for augmented reality applications.

docs.text: This project automates the process of collecting spectral data across a 2D surface using two motorized Thorlabs ELL17 linear stages and an Ocean Optics HR400 spectrometer.
